env.world: finite-population design-based randomization world: a finite unit type `V` with a known directed interference graph (self-loops allowed) and the unit-level product Bernoulli assignment law on `Ω = V → Bool`, carried by `FiniteDesign` with the finite-sum `E`/`Var`/`Cov` algebra.
env.notes: This is the single highest-leverage reuse decision: the paper's only randomness is the unit-level product Bernoulli assignment, which is exactly `bernoulliDesign p hp0 hp1 : FiniteDesign (V → Bool)` (constant `p i = p`). Cross-coordinate independence — the engine of every orthogonality, block-independence and variance computation in the paper — is then STRUCTURAL (`prodDesign`), not an assumption: `FiniteDesign.E_prod_apply`, `E_prod_apply₂`, `Cov_prod_apply_of_ne`, `Var_prod_apply`, `Var_prod_linear_comb` (ProductVariance) and the block generalizations `E_prod_block_mul`, `Cov_prod_disjoint_zero` (ProductBlock) give the disjoint-block factorization the complete-directed-block arguments need. `\mathbb E_Z` is `FiniteDesign.E` of this design; `P_Z` is the design itself. env.world: design-based decision-theoretic world: GRAPH-AWARE estimators measurable in the full observed data `(G, Z, (Y_i^obs))`, their design mean squared error at a fixed model, the worst case over a model class, and the minimax (inf over estimators) risk.
env.notes: REVISED (round 2, FLAG-world-arity): an estimator is GRAPH-AWARE — `Estimator V := (V → V → Bool) → (V → Bool) → (V → ℝ) → ℝ` (known graph, assignment, observed outcome vector), matching the core's `\widehat\tau_n` symbol (`refs: [G_n, Z, Y_i^{obs}]`) and def:minimax-risk's 'measurable in `(G_n, Z, {Y_i^obs})`'. The graph is NOT fixed inside the risk functional: `riskAt` COMPOSES the single global estimator with the model's own graph, `riskAt p M est = (bernoulliDesign …).mse (fun z => est (edgeFn M) z (obsOutcome M z)) (tte M)`, where `edgeFn M := fun j i => decide (M.edge j i)` uses the class structure's existing `decEdge` field. The inf–sup is therefore the core's: ONE estimator faces every `(G_n, c)` in the class, and `snipeEstimator β p : Estimator V` (which reads its neighborhoods off its graph argument) is one admissible global competitor, so the middle term of thm:bounded-outcome-degree-frontier is literally `worstRisk … (snipeClipped B β p)`. The per-model risk is exactly `D.mse est μ = D.E (fun z => (est z - μ)^2)` with `D = bernoulliDesign`, `μ = τ_n`; `mse_eq_var_add_bias_sq`, `mse_eq_var_of_unbiased`, `var_le_mse`, `Unbiased` are all reused verbatim (the unclipped-SNIPE branch is `mse = Var` after unbiasedness; the clipping branch uses `mse_nonneg` + a pointwise projection bound). Surveyed and bypass-justified: `Causalean.Experimentation.DesignBased.worstRisk` / `IsMinimaxOn` (Optimality/Minimax.lean) minimize over DESIGNS at a fixed estimator, not over ESTIMATORS at a fixed design — the wrong quantifier order for this paper; `ProbabilityTheory.minimaxRisk` (Mathlib Decision/Risk) is kernel/loss-shaped over a general `Kernel`-valued experiment and would force a measure-theoretic re-encoding of the finite design.

def:exposed-order.statement_sketch: `bernoulliContrast p r = (1-p)^r - (-p)^r` (`Δ_r(p)`); `effBeta β d = min β d`; `kStar d β p = ` the largest `r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (effBeta β d)` with `bernoulliContrast p r ≠ 0`, as a `Finset.max'` over a set nonempty because `Δ_1(p) = 1`; `kStar 0 β p = 0`.

Pure arithmetic construction; `Finset.max'` with the `Δ_1(p) = 1` nonemptiness witness keeps `kStar` computable and total, avoiding a junk-value branch.

def:zero-degree-conventions.statement_sketch: `ZeroDegreeConventions : Prop := effBeta β 0 = 0 ∧ kStar 0 β p = 0 ∧ blockScore 0 = 0 ∧ blockEnergy 0 = 0 ∧ blockRepresenter 0 = 0` — a named `def : Prop` recording the degree-zero boundary values, proved by `Finset.sum_empty`/`Finset.Icc_self`-style `decide`/`simp` in the accompanying lemma `zeroDegreeConventions_holds`.
def:zero-degree-conventions.notes: SYNC-BACK F2: moved from `Basic.lean` to `Helpers/BlockScore.lean` because the proposition definitionally mentions `blockScore`, `blockEnergy`, `blockRepresenter`, and `blockRawCoef`; keeping it in Basic would create an import cycle. def:model-class.statement_sketch: `structure ModelClass (V) (d β : ℕ) (B : ℝ) where edge : V → V → Prop; decEdge : DecidableRel edge; coef : V → Finset V → ℝ; supported : ∀ i S, ¬ S ⊆ nbhd edge i → coef i S = 0; degree_le : BoundedDegree edge d; low_order : LowOrder coef β; mass_le : BoundedCoeffMass edge coef B` — the carrier data `(G_n, c)` plus ONE Prop field per member atom, each typed by that atom's `def : Prop`.
def:model-class.notes: The sup in the minimax risk ranges over terms of this structure; it is the `Y_max`-normalized ℓ¹ model class. Its `members` are exactly the core's `by_member_properties = [ass:bounded-degree, ass:low-order, ass:bounded-coefficient-mass]` — the FLATTENED atom list, one structure field per member atom (`degree_le`, `low_order`, `mass_le`), which is the normative mapping (a member must be an assumption atom, never a component class). Semantically this is still exactly `G_n ∈ 𝒢_{n,d} ∧ c ∈ 𝒞_{n,d,β}(B)`, and the component classes of def:graph-class / def:coefficient-class remain reusable building blocks: F2 should emit the two round-trip abbreviations `ModelClass.ofComponents (g : GraphClass V d) (c : CoeffClass g.edge β B) : ModelClass V d β B` and the projections `M.toGraphClass`, `M.toCoeffClass`, so any construction phrased over the components (notably def:block-family's `blockGraph`/`blockSchedule`) transports to this structure in one step and consumers never pattern-match twice. The neighborhood-support field `supported` is structural (part of the schedule TYPE `\mathbb R^{{(i,S) : S ⊆ N_i}}` in the core's symbol table), not an atomized assumption, so it is an inline carrier field and not a member.

def:snipe-score.statement_sketch: `snipeScore (G : V → V → Bool) β p i z = ∑ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (effBeta β d), (bernoulliContrast p r / (p*(1-p))^r) * ∑ S ∈ (nbhdB G i).powerset.filter (·.card = r), ∏ j ∈ S, ((if z j then (1:ℝ) else 0) - p)` — the graph is the Bool-valued relation the estimator RECEIVES (see def:minimax-risk), and `nbhdB G i = univ.filter (fun j => G j i)`, related to the class structures' `nbhd M.edge i` by the bridge lemma `nbhdB (edgeFn M) i = nbhd M.edge i`.
def:snipe-score.notes: REVISED (round 2, FLAG-world-arity): the score now reads its neighborhoods off the graph ARGUMENT rather than off an ambient fixed graph, so `snipeEstimator` is a legal global `Estimator V`. Search trace: `lean_local_search 'snipe'`, 'score', 'representer', 'weight'; read `../doc/API.md` §18 (HT/Estimators/Exposure tables). Result: not found — Causalean's design-based estimators are Horvitz–Thompson (`htTotal`/`htMean`/`htEffect`, inverse-propensity weights on exposure indicators) and Hájek; SNIPE's centered-monomial polynomial score is a different weight family. Bypass-justified vs `DesignBased/HT/Estimator.lean`: SNIPE is not an IPW estimator (its weights are signed and can exceed 1/π), so the HT unbiasedness lemma `E_htTotal` does not apply; unbiasedness here comes from the block representer identity instead.

def:snipe-estimator.statement_sketch: `snipeEstimator β p : Estimator V := fun G z y => (n:ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i, y i * snipeScore G β p i z` — a function of the KNOWN GRAPH, the assignment and the OBSERVED outcome vector, in the exact argument order of the `Estimator V` abbreviation, so it is one admissible global competitor in the inf of def:minimax-risk; `snipeClipped B β p : Estimator V := fun G z y => max (-B) (min B (snipeEstimator β p G z y))`.
def:snipe-estimator.notes: REVISED (round 2, FLAG-world-arity): the estimator is now graph-aware (previously the graph was a fixed ambient parameter, which is not one global competitor). The composition with a model's own graph is `snipeEstimator β p (edgeFn M) z (obsOutcome M z)`, which `riskAt` performs; the neighborhood bridge `nbhdB (edgeFn M) i = nbhd M.edge i` (def:snipe-score) turns every score computation back into the class-structure form in one rewrite, so no downstream variance or unbiasedness lemma changes shape. def:minimax-risk.statement_sketch: GRAPH-AWARE (revised round 2): `Estimator V := (V → V → Bool) → (V → Bool) → (V → ℝ) → ℝ` — the estimator takes the KNOWN graph, the assignment, and the observed outcome vector, exactly the core's `\widehat\tau_n` measurable in `(G_n, Z, {Y_i^{obs}})`. `edgeFn (M : ModelClass V d β B) : V → V → Bool := fun j i => decide (M.edge j i)` (available from the structure's `decEdge` field). `riskAt p M est = (bernoulliDesign …).mse (fun z => est (edgeFn M) z (obsOutcome M z)) (tte M)` (REUSING `FiniteDesign.mse`), i.e. the risk COMPOSES the single global estimator with the model's OWN graph rather than fixing a graph inside the estimator; `worstRisk … est = sSup {riskAt p M est | M : ModelClass …}`; `minimaxRisk … = sInf {worstRisk … est | est : Estimator V, Measurable-in-outcomes and BddAbove {riskAt p M est | M}}`. The bounded-range condition explicitly removes unbounded-risk competitors from the real-valued `sSup`; this is the paper's ordinary extended supremum represented in ℝ without the conditionally-complete junk value.
def:minimax-risk.notes: REVISED (round 2, FLAG-world-arity): the round-1 arity `Estimator V := (V → Bool) → (V → ℝ) → ℝ` was graph-blind, which fixed `G` inside `riskAt` and silently changed the inf–sup problem (a different estimator per graph) and made `snipeEstimator G` not a single admissible global competitor. The graph argument is now part of the estimator's input, so the inf ranges over ONE rule facing every `(G_n, c)` in the sup — the core's problem — and `snipeEstimator β p`, `snipeClipped B β p`, `snipeClippedBdd B β p` are each ONE `Estimator V`, making `minimaxRisk ≤ worstRisk … (snipeClipped B β p)` a direct `sInf` bound (`minimaxRisk_le`) instead of a per-graph argument. The graph is passed as a Bool-valued relation `V → V → Bool` (not `V → V → Prop`) so it is a first-class datum with no `DecidableRel` instance argument to carry through the inf; F2 emits `nbhdB (G : V → V → Bool) i := univ.filter (fun j => G j i)` together with the bridge `nbhdB (edgeFn M) i = nbhd M.edge i` (a `Finset.filter_congr` on `decide_eq_true_iff`), so every neighborhood lemma proved for `nbhd` transports in one rewrite and the class structures keep their existing `edge`/`decEdge` fields UNCHANGED. Two consequences recorded for F2: (i) the upper-bound branches of thm:bounded-outcome-degree-frontier / thm:degree-frontier are `worstRisk … (snipeClipped …)` with the same estimator term on both classes; (ii) in the converse, both prior mixtures are supported on schedules carrying the SAME graph `blockGraph n d`, so the estimator's graph argument is a CONSTANT across the two hypotheses and the Le Cam two-point reduction applies to `fun z y => est (blockGraph n d) z y` verbatim. def:block-family.statement_sketch: `blockFamilyBundle` mechanically exposes the linked tuple `(blockCount n d, activeCount n d, activeShare n d, blockGraph n d, blockSchedulePrior n d β B p σ)`. Here `blockCount n d = n / d`, `activeCount = blockCount * d`, `activeShare = (activeCount : ℝ)/n`; `blockGraph n d` is the complete directed block graph with loops and isolated remainder; `cosSqDensity s u = s⁻¹ * Real.cos (π*u/(2*s))^2 * indicator |u| ≤ s`; `tiltAmplitude = B * min (2*H)⁻¹ (4*π)⁻¹ * min 1 (√(A_d/m))`; `blockSchedule σ (U : Fin m → ℝ)` has `c i T = U (blk i) * 1{T = ∅} + σ * δ * blockRawCoef T`; `blockSchedulePrior` is the pushforward prior on these schedules; `blockPriorLaw σ` is the compressed sufficient-statistic law with density `p_Z(z) * ∏_b cosSqDensity s (y b - σ*δ*h_d (z restricted to block b))` w.r.t. `count ⊗ volume^m`; and `priorPredictiveLaw σ : Measure ((Fin n → Bool) × (Fin n → ℝ))` is the pushforward of `blockPriorLaw σ` under the map that repeats each active block outcome across its units and assigns outcome zero to inactive units.
def:block-family.notes: Search trace: `lean_local_search 'prior'`, 'leastFavourable', 'fuzzy', 'cos', 'cosSq', 'bump' → nothing matching a continuous least-favourable BASELINE prior; `Estimation/MinimaxATE/Reduction/Bump.lean` (`l2sq_bump`, Rademacher ±δ bump) is the analogous module — same two-mixture ±σ tilt pattern, but with FINITE hypotheses and a χ² certificate, so only the packaging pattern transfers. REVISED (round 3, FLAG-finite-mixture): `Causalean.Stat.mixture`/`mixtureReal_le` (Minimax/Mixture.lean) is NO LONGER claimed as a reuse for the realizability step, and `Causalean.Stat.Minimax.Mixture` is removed from this node's modules. Verified against the source (`Grep 'mixtureReal' ../Causalean/Stat/Minimax/` → `Mixture.lean:53 theorem mixtureReal_le (w : ι → ℝ≥0∞) (hw : ∑ i, w i = 1) …`, `[Fintype ι]`): it bounds the `.real` MASS of a FINITE `Fintype`-indexed convex combination of measures, whereas the baseline prior here is the CONTINUOUS product `⊗_{b ≤ m} f_s(u)du` over `U : Fin m → ℝ` and the quantity to dominate is an integrated RISK. The realizability step is therefore a LOCAL lemma, planned in full rather than adapted: (R0) `prior_integrated_risk_le_worstRisk` in this same file — `∫ riskAt p (blockSchedule σ U) est ∂(blockBaselinePrior s m) ≤ worstRisk p est` for every admissible `est`. Its ingredients are all already planned here: the admissibility lemma of this node puts `blockSchedule σ U ∈ ModelClass V d β B` for EVERY `U` in the support (`|U_b| + δ∑_T|h_{d,T}| ≤ B/2 + κBH ≤ B`), so `riskAt p (blockSchedule σ U) est ≤ worstRisk p est` pointwise by the reused `le_worstRisk` API lemma of def:minimax-risk; then `MeasureTheory.integral_mono_ae` + `integral_const` + `IsProbabilityMeasure` on the prior finish it. F2 must emit the prior as a genuine probability measure — `blockBaselinePrior s m : Measure (Fin m → ℝ) := Measure.pi (fun _ => volume.withDensity (fun u => ENNReal.ofReal (cosSqDensity s u)))` with `∫ cosSqDensity s = 1` (the same closed-form `intervalIntegral` computation (C2) needs) and `IsProbabilityMeasure` derived through `MeasureTheory.isProbabilityMeasure_pi` — since (R0)'s `integral_const` step and the Fubini step (R1) below both consume it. (R1), the companion identity that makes (R0) bite: `E_{P_σ}[(est − σθ)²] = ∫ riskAt p (blockSchedule σ U) est ∂(blockBaselinePrior s m)`, i.e. the prior-predictive expectation equals the prior-integrated design risk, by Fubini on the explicit `count ⊗ volume^m` density (the same `Measure.prod`/`Measure.pi` idiom as (C1) in S4 — the finite assignment sum comes out first, then the `U`-integral). Together (R1)+(R0) are exactly the paper's sentence 'each prior is supported on deterministic schedules in the smaller model class, so its integrated risk cannot exceed the corresponding worst-case risk', with no finite-mixture machinery anywhere. Observed data reduction (IMPORTANT and recorded for F2): under this family the observed outcomes are constant within each active block and zero off it, so the sufficient observed statistic is `(Z, (Y_b)_{b ≤ m}) ∈ (V → Bool) × ℝ^m`; the law is written directly on that product with an explicit density, which keeps the whole converse inside `Measure.prod`/`Measure.pi` + `withDensity` and avoids any conditional-kernel machinery. REVISED (round 2): that explicit density presentation is now LOAD-BEARING, not merely convenient — both `blockPriorLaw (+1)` and `blockPriorLaw (-1)` are `λ.withDensity`-of a common dominating `λ = count(V → Bool) ⊗ volume^m`, which is the hypothesis shape of the local affinity-to-TV lemma (C0) in S4; the two laws are NOT mutually absolutely continuous (the cosine-square baselines are compactly supported and the two tilts translate them apart), so F2/F3 must never phrase this step through a mutual RN derivative `dP₊/dP₋`. F2 should therefore emit `blockPriorDensity σ : (V → Bool) × (Fin m → ℝ) → ℝ` as a standalone nonneg. measurable function together with `blockPriorLaw σ = λ.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (blockPriorDensity σ x))` and `∫ blockPriorDensity σ ∂λ = 1`, so (C0) applies verbatim. REVISED (round 2, FLAG-world-arity): both mixtures use the SAME graph `blockGraph n d`, so under the graph-aware `Estimator V` the converse fixes `est (edgeFn (blockGraph n d))` once and the two-point reduction sees an ordinary data-only estimator — the graph argument carries no information distinguishing the hypotheses.
